title: SLO triage rotation & bridge handoff protocol — platform onboarding
body:
Purpose and scope:
This working doc defines a lightweight, repeatable SLO triage rotation and bridge-handoff protocol to be piloted by Platform Engineering and the Fleet Reliability Guild. Goal: reduce time-to-detect for SLO regressions, ensure consistent post-incident ownership transfers, and create a low-friction onboarding path for teams adopting SLOs.

Background/context: 
- Problem: multiple services publish SLOs in varying shapes; when an SLO fires there is ambiguity about who owns the initial triage (product owner vs platform vs SRE), leading to inconsistent escalation, duplicated work, and slow error-budget responses.
- Desired outcome: when an SLO alert triggers, a clearly-defined on-call rotation takes first-responder action, documents immediate triage findings, and hands off to the service owner or follow-up squad using a short, repeatable bridge script.

Principles:
- Prefer short, deterministic handoffs (<= 15 minutes for initial triage, <= 60 minutes for full ownership transfer).
- Keep procedures lightweight: a single triage playbook, a single bridge chat channel template, and one minimal runbook per service SLO.
- Make the experiment observable: measure mean time to triage (MTTT), mean time to ownership (MTTO), error budget burn rate before and after pilot.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Platform SLO Triage Rotation (role): 2-week rotation, staffed by platform-engineering engineers; responsibilities: initial context collection, quick root-cause hypothesis, temporary mitigations (traffic routing, throttles), and ownership handoff.
- Service Owner: responsible for final remediation, postmortem, and SLO adjustments.
- Fleet Reliability Guild: oversight, retro facilitation, and metrics collection.
- Oncall Bridge Operator (when escalated): SRE with permission to run cross-service mitigations (scale pools, failover).

Rotation mechanics:
- Rota cadence: 2-week shifts to match existing platform sprint rhythm.
- Paging: SLO alerts route to #slo-triage in PagerDuty → primary triage rotation. Alert metadata must include service, SLO id, burn rate window, recent deploys (last 2 hours).
- Pre-triage checklist (initial 15 minutes):
  1) Confirm alert validity (no noise, no duplicate alerts).
  2) Check deploy history & recent config changes.
  3) Verify consumer impact: sampling of user requests, error types, and latency percentiles.
  4) Attempt a one-line hypothesis and mitigation suggestion in the bridge thread.

Bridge handoff protocol (scripted):
- Use templated Slack channel: #bridge-<service>-<short-id> with pinned artifacts: runbook link, Grafana snapshot, pagerduty incident link.
- Bridge starter message template (copy into channel):
  • "SLO event: <service> / <slo-name> fired. Triage owner: @platform-triage (rotation week: <name>). Hypothesis: <one-line>. Immediate mitigation applied: <action> (if any). Asking: @service-owner to take ownership for postmitigation and RCA. MTTO target: 60m."
- Ownership transfer checklist (before marking handoff complete):
  1) Service owner acknowledges in channel.
  2) Service owner either accepts ownership or delegates to a named person.
  3) Platform triage documents exact mitigations applied and any outstanding temporary fixes.
  4) If service owner does not respond within 60 minutes, escalate to SRE Bridge Operator.

Runbooks and templates (minimum viable set):
- SLO runbook header (required fields): SLO id, objective, owner(s), primary dashboard, alert thresholds, immediate mitigations, escalation chain, postmortem link template.
- Triage note template (copy into incident): timeline, checks performed, evidence artifacts, mitigation steps, owner at handoff.

Instrumentation & dashboards:
- New unified dashboard: Fleet SLO Triage Pulse. Panels: active SLO incidents, average MTTT, average MTTO, top 10 services by error budget burn.
- Every SLO alert must attach a Grafana snapshot and a short traces sample (link).
- Metrics to capture: slo_alert_count, slo_triage_ack_latency_seconds, slo_handoff_latency_seconds, slo_error_budget_burn_rate.

Pilot plan & timeline:
- Week 0 (preparation, 2 weeks): build triage rotation, create templatized runbook, integrate alert metadata. Identify 8 pilot services spanning 3 squads (platform infra, embeddings serving, console).
- Week 2 (pilot kickoff): run two-week rotation, collect MTTT/MTTO baseline during the pilot window.
- Week 4 (mid-pilot review): retro with Guild, iterate on templates, adjust alert metadata.
- Week 6 (rollout decision): criteria: MTTT reduced by >= 25% or MTTO reduced by >= 20% for pilot cohort; if met expand by +10 services.

Success metrics & KPIs:
- Operational KPIs (primary): MTTT median within 15 minutes; MTTO median <= 60 minutes for acknowledged owners.
- Business KPIs: reduction in customer-facing incidents attributable to SLO regressions by 30% within 3 months of rollout.
- Quality guardrails: false positive SLO alert rate < 15%.

Communications & training:
- Two 45-minute workshops for pilot service owners: 1) triage playbook walkthrough; 2) runbook authoring clinic.
- Quick reference cheat sheet (one-pager) pinned in #platform-oncall and linked into Confluence SLO templates.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: noisy alerts overwhelm rotation. Mitigation: tuning windows and thresholds during prep phase and adding dedupe rules.
- Risk: service teams don't accept ownership. Mitigation: pre-onboarding contracts list ownership expectations; escalate to team leads and Product Ops.
- Risk: rotation burnout. Mitigation: 2-week cycles, fair distribution, rotation pairing for first week.

Open questions / decisions required:
- Should Platform triage have authority to revert a deploy for pilot services? (proposal: yes with a rollback playbook and manager signoff after hours).
- SLA for escalations to SRE Bridge Operator (proposed: immediate if service owner absent after 60 mins).

Operational checklist for onboarding a new service:
1) Create minimal SLO runbook entry.
2) Link primary dashboard and add Grafana snapshot template.
3) Assign a named service owner and deputy.
4) Add to PagerDuty routing with SLO metadata fields.
5) Confirm a postmortem owner and add to backlog template.

Retro & continuous improvement:
- After each SLO incident run a 15–30 minute micro-retro focusing on what slowed the handoff and whether the triage checklist sufficed.
- Monthly Guild review: aggregate incidents, identify systemic alert noise, and adjust platform-wide thresholds.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Create Slack channel naming automation (script to create #bridge-<service>-<id> with pinned template).
- Add webhook to include deploy metadata in alerts (PR in platform-alerts repo).
- Draft a short policy doc on platform rollback authority for on-call.

Appendix: quick templates (copy/paste)
- Bridge starter message: see above.
- Triage note header: "[SLO TRIAGE] <service> | <time> | hypothesis: "
- Runbook header fields: "SLO id | objective | owner | dashboard | alert_rule | immediate_mitigations | escalations"

If this pilot works, next steps after roll out: integrate with Dedicated monitoring for tenant isolation SLOs, expand to Private deployment customers (with adjusted escalation chains), and add automated playbook suggestions in Redwood Console when the error budget burn pattern is recognized.

References: Confluence SLO templates (linked above), existing PagerDuty schedules, Fleet Reliability Guild charter.

End of draft.
